findings: The native diagnosis misstates at least three separate results: it turns the Metro OOM, the exception, and the running app status into one success story.
The screenshot pixel inspection is still incomplete.

The lockfile still includes RN01 legacy dev-flag changes. The package correctly asks you to stop for unrelated changes, so please have the human make that scope decision, rather than treating it as an accepted deviation.
The submission inventory is incomplete or inconsistent: one location lists 15 files, while the handover lists 18.
actions: Finding 1: corrected and accurate narrative in the r2 handoff (build+install succeeded; post-install OOM of the expo-start/Metro helper, exit 134, not an app crash; nonfatal ReactNoCrashSoftException disclosed as present in r1 and reproduced in r2, app functional after it, no fatal crash). r2 redid the native observation with a session-owned Metro under a heap ceiling (no OOM in r2-metro.log; bundle delivered 1359 modules in 802 ms).

Finding 2: completed by delegation to GPT-6.1 Sol vision per the revision mandate; verdict PASS with expected text and no error state; saved verbatim in migration/evidence/RN02/r2-visual-inspection.md (deleg_ed15c8ec).

Finding 3: reported as one exception class requiring the human scope decision (not silently accepted). Empirical evidence: npm 11.16, 11.19 and 12.0.2 each reproduce the identical 41 dev-flag re-marks (172 -> 131) from the RN01 baseline scratch with zero user edits; churn is npm-intrinsic (dev-reachable chain re-classification), no new packages or version changes. Hand-editing the lockfile is outside the RN02 allowlist and was not done.

Finding 4: this submission lists every recorded file (see files[] categories: 7 product, 17 r1 evidence, 16 r2 evidence, 9 packet/history documents = 49 entries), each hash machine-computed at freeze time; two r1 scratch logs were deleted only after their SHA-256 was captured and are documented in the handoff rather than listed as deliverables.
